title: Savings Incubator: Priority Grid & Field Experiment Pipeline for Batching/Caching/Quant
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, low-friction pipeline to prioritize and run field experiments that reduce per-token inference cost across hosted and dedicated deployments by combining batching, KV/prefix caching, and model quantization profiles. This initiative (Savings Incubator) will produce a prioritization grid, a templated experiment harness, and an operational playbook for safe rollouts and guardrails.

What success looks like (OKRs):
- OKR 1: Reduce hosted per-token elastic cost by 12% on average for conversational workloads within 8 weeks of rollouts for initial customers.
- OKR 2: Establish a reproducible experiment pipeline used by at least 3 product teams for A/B field trials within one cycle.
- OKR 3: Surface cost/quality decision boundaries into Console (per-route recommendations) and ship first iteration of automated suggestion engine.

Scope & deliverables:
1) Prioritization grid: taxonomy that scores candidate optimizations by expected savings, QA risk, rollout friction, and customer opt-in complexity.
2) Experiment harness: parameterized job that can run on Dedicated and Hosted runners to evaluate batching window, cache TTL/prefix heuristics, and quant profiles across representative prompt sets. Includes synthetic replay + live shadowing mode.
3) Instrumentation: standardized metrics (token-cost delta, quality-regression rate, latency p50/p95, error uplift, customer-facing quality score) wired into Console dashboards and alerts.
4) Playbook & rollback policy: clear checklists for canary size, QA thresholds, automatic fallback triggers, and customer communication template.
5) Starter runbook and results for two cross-product pilots (Chat frontend + Search rerank).

Hypotheses to test (examples):
- H1: 8–16ms batching windows increase throughput with <0.5% quality regression for chat-style prompts and give >=9% token cost saving.
- H2: Prefix-aware KV caching with 30s TTL on short sessions reduces repeated decoding by >=15% on median conversational sessions.
- H3: 4-bit quant profile for high-latency tolerant routes reduces per-token compute cost by ~25% with acceptable quality delta for summarization tasks.

Risks & mitigation:
- Quality regressions: have labeled prompt-suite and automated eval gating; all rollouts start as shadow.
- Observability gaps: Add sampling hooks and token-level attribution on rollout paths before live canary.
- Customer trust: provide per-route opt-out and clear comms; include safety review for quantization on PII-handling workloads.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Marcus Nguyen (Console integrations), Priya Sharma (Customer Success liaison)
- Engineering: runtime (Alina Gomez), infra (Liam O'Connor assigned), observability (Chen Wei)
- Research/Applied ML: quantization and evals (Dr. Mateo Ruiz)
- Security & Legal: for data residency and KMS implications

Success metrics (tracked daily):
- Weekly aggregated token-cost delta (hosted + dedicated) reported in Console (goal: -12%).
- Quality regression rate (test-labeled prompts) must remain <0.8% for any canary.
- Mean latency p95 change <= +10ms for target routes.
- Number of product teams adopting the experiment harness >= 3 by end of cycle.
